metadata.course_title: Data Centers: From Digital Services to Physical Infrastructure

scope_limits: Every slide was reviewed as text using the current full-content packets, including complete active script bodies, imported transcripts, all quiz choices/keys/feedback, static-figure labels and available video text inventories. Duplicate transcript/cue forms were compared programmatically; their only differences were line-wrap hyphen spacing.

No perceptual listening of narration or imported audio was performed, and no audio was played aloud. Audio realization, pronunciation, transcription fidelity and timing are not certified by this audit.

One representative current frame from each of the five generated teaching videos was viewed, plus the M2S6 editable state/timing source. This is conceptual sampling, not a complete encoded-frame, continuity, timing or fullscreen/playback audit.

No source-recording frames were newly viewed in this audit; original-video visual conclusions rely on the supplied reviewed inventories. Static figures were text-reviewed, not visually re-approved here.

Primary sources were opened and read for material corrections and selected numerical/current claims. No exhaustive link, copyright, electrical design, environmental compliance, legal or product-specification certification is claimed.
No LMS session, SCORM completion, mobile UI, quiz persistence or accessibility behavior was tested. Earlier timing-only and connector audits are not treated as proof of content accuracy.
The live Academy URL returned a JavaScript shell; local adjacent AICC course/scripts verified scope. Enrollment and live course equivalence were not verified.

quiz_review.note: Four associations are distinguishable; global cloud is a hyperscale example, not an exclusive definition. Existing feedback appropriately allows overlap.

key.match: Located near end-users to reduce latency
Built and used by a single organization
Shared facility where tenants bring their own equipment

quiz_review.note: Choice c is the best answer; feedback also includes networking and facility support.
Choice b matches the core cloud definition; public internet and multiple sites are correctly not mandatory.
Choice d; distractors are weak but unambiguous. No need to add difficulty merely for its own sake.
Choice b; conventional AC-input scope avoids falsely excluding DC-fed architectures.
Choice c; expansion card role is accurate for the stated examples.
Choice b; distinguishes panel width from hole spacing, depth and height.
Possible hardware sizes, but the stated illustrated mapping is not supplied by current teaching; F01.
Choice c; feedback correctly conditions useful heat on temperature, distance and infrastructure and does not promise lower PUE.
Choice b; context distinguishes energy-management zombies from malware and legitimate standby capacity.
Choice b; workload-dependent mixed cooling is defensible. Distractors are broad but not ambiguous.
Plausible associations, but several exact trends are not taught and heat reuse is awkwardly categorized; F13.

key.match: Distributed or regional deployment matched to local constraints
Shift toward modular and hybrid architectures
Direct investment and clean energy sourcing

imported_recording_review.status: No material factual correction required at this level.
imported_recording_review.assessment: Systems overview is broad and examples should not be read as a universal facility bill of materials. Generic supporting caption is adequate for the role.
Edge/modularity and carrier-neutral shorthand remain misleading; later M1S8 helps but the immediate caption does not counter them.

imported_recording_review.status: Existing correction is substantially sufficient in text.
imported_recording_review.assessment: The recording conflates air handlers with CRACs and UPSs with battery banks. The adjacent caption explicitly distinguishes CRAC/CRAH and a complete UPS, and M2S6/M2S9 reinforce the system roles. A named environmental goal is not proof of lower lifecycle emissions.

imported_recording_review.status: Existing correction is substantially sufficient; add definition F11.
imported_recording_review.assessment: The adjacent note directly corrects continuously-running generators, qualifies startup/supported load, treats rack densities as examples and qualifies fuel emissions. M2S6 gives a sound backup sequence. N+1 remains unexplained.

imported_recording_review.status: Existing correction is substantially sufficient; optional F16.
imported_recording_review.assessment: The note explicitly rejects the claim that each cooling level creates redundancy and conditions temperature/efficiency claims. Clarifying inlet conditions would help. Immersion benefits remain design-dependent.
The current variation caveat is useful but should explicitly counter the failure/power ranking and unsupported server-majority claim; redundancy is not a guarantee.

imported_recording_review.status: Existing correction is strong in text; glossary error F02 is separate.
imported_recording_review.assessment: The source says 44.45 centimeters for 1U and treats 19 inches as rail separation. Adjacent caption plus M3S4/M3S5 clearly correct both, including U versus performance. This audit does not assert that every viewer notices an outside-video note in fullscreen.

imported_recording_review.status: Existing correction is mostly sufficient; F05 also applies.
imported_recording_review.assessment: Heat reuse does not recover every kWh usefully; M4S13 fixes this well. Quantum requirements differ by platform, and local hosting is not automatic compliance or resilience. The unsupported majority-of-workloads statement should not be retained as a fact.
Current caveats are too generic for DCIM workload-management and ISO distinction; market-share claims need a decisive non-use note.

imported_recording_review.status: Existing correction partly sufficient; strengthen via F07; verify F17.
imported_recording_review.assessment: Bare-metal multiple-app support and variable utilization are already corrected. Shared-host failure, coexistence of containers and VMs, and the microservers/microservices discrepancy remain.
